stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
The source distinguishes the extension-allowing criterion from the usual valuative criterion of a unique lift without extension.

Let $S$ be a scheme.
Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces over $S$.
Assume
\begin{enumerate}
\item the morphism $f$ is quasi-separated, and
\item the morphism $f$ satisfies the uniqueness
part of the valuative criterion.
\end{enumerate}
Then $f$ is separated.

reason: Valuative uniqueness implies that Δ_{X/Y} satisfies the existence criterion: any pair of lifts over Spec A agree. Quasi-separatedness makes the diagonal quasi-compact; the previously proved criterion yields its universal closedness, and its locally finite-type separated monomorphism structure then makes it finite and hence a closed immersion.

stage_b_reviewed_content.statement:
The source distinguishes the extension-allowing criterion from the usual valuative criterion of a unique lift without extension.

Let $S$ be a scheme. Let $f : X \to Y$ be a morphism of algebraic spaces
over $S$. Assume $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Then the
following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item $f$ is separated and universally closed,
\item the valuative criterion holds as in Definition
\ref{definition-valuative-criterion},
\item given any commutative solid diagram
$$
\xymatrix{
\Spec(K) \ar[r] \ar[d] & X \ar[d] \\
\Spec(A) \ar[r] \ar@{-->}[ru] & Y
}
$$
where $A$ is a valuation ring with field of fractions $K$, there exists
a unique dotted arrow, i.e., $f$ satisfies the valuative
criterion as in
Schemes, Definition \ref{schemes-definition-valuative-criterion}.
\end{enumerate}
